title: UGC Opens Applications for NSPG and Ishan Uday Scholarships Worth Up to ₹1.5 Lakh Per Year
excerpt: The University Grants Commission is accepting applications for two major scholarship schemes through the National Scholarship Portal — one for postgraduate students across India and another for undergraduates from the Northeast.
body:
• The National Scholarship for Postgraduate Studies (NSPG) offers ₹15,000 per month for two years to first-year PG students under 30, with 10,000 scholarships awarded annually
  • Ishan Uday provides ₹5,400–₹7,800 per month to first-year undergraduate students from India's eight Northeastern states, with a family income cap of ₹4.5 lakh per year
  • Both schemes accept applications through the National Scholarship Portal (scholarships.gov.in), with the registration window open since June 1 and most deadlines falling on October 31, 2026
  • Students must complete a One-Time Registration (OTR) with Aadhaar-based face authentication before applying — a step that frequently causes rejections if done incorrectly

The University Grants Commission has opened applications for two of its flagship scholarship programmes for the 2026–27 academic year: the National Scholarship for Postgraduate Studies (NSPG) and the Ishan Uday Special Scholarship Scheme for the North Eastern Region. Both are live on the National Scholarship Portal and will remain open until October 31, 2026, according to the portal's official schedule.

The NSPG targets students entering their first postgraduate degree at a recognised Indian institution. Each awardee receives ₹15,000 per month for 10 months a year over two years — a total of up to ₹3 lakh across the programme's duration. Approximately 10,000 scholarships are distributed each year. Applicants must be under 30, enrolled full-time in their first year, and must not hold an existing PG degree. The scheme is implemented by the UGC under the Ministry of Education.

Ishan Uday: Bridging the Higher Education Gap in the Northeast

The Ishan Uday scholarship is a separate UGC initiative focused on students from eight Northeastern states: Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, and Tripura. It awards 10,000 fresh scholarships annually to first-year undergraduate students who passed Class XII from a school within the region.

Students pursuing general degree courses receive ₹5,400 per month, while those enrolled in technical, medical, or paramedical programmes get ₹7,800 per month. The family income ceiling is ₹4.5 lakh per annum. Institutions must be recognised under Section 2(f) of the UGC Act with valid NAAC accreditation, or classified as Institutes of National Importance.

"The Ishan Uday Scholarship Scheme is a significant step towards bridging the educational gap in India's NE region, ensuring that students have the financial support they need to achieve their aspirations."

— UGC, official scheme description

How to Apply: OTR Registration Is the Critical First Step

Both scholarships require applicants to complete a One-Time Registration on the National Scholarship Portal at scholarships.gov.in. The process, introduced in the 2024–25 cycle, involves registering a mobile number, verifying via OTP, then downloading two apps — AadhaarFaceRD and the NSP OTR app — to complete Aadhaar-based face authentication. Only after the OTR ID is generated can students log in and fill their scholarship application.

Common documents needed include Aadhaar card, income certificate issued by the relevant state authority, admission proof, bank passbook for Direct Benefit Transfer linkage, and mark sheets of qualifying exams. Ishan Uday applicants also require a domicile certificate and a notarised affidavit confirming they are not receiving any other scholarship. Applications can be saved as drafts before final submission.

The registration window opened on June 1, 2026. For most UGC schemes, the final submission deadline is October 31, with institute-level verification closing on November 15 and state-level verification wrapping up by November 30. Scholarship disbursements typically begin between January and March of the following year through the Public Financial Management System (PFMS).

What It Means for the Diaspora

For Indian families abroad whose children are considering undergraduate or postgraduate studies in India, these schemes represent substantial financial support. The NSPG's ₹1.5 lakh annual assistance can offset a meaningful share of tuition and living costs at public universities, while Ishan Uday specifically addresses the needs of families with roots in the Northeast — a community with a growing diaspora presence in cities across Southeast Asia, the Gulf, and the United States.

What's Next

Students who meet the eligibility criteria should complete their OTR registration immediately rather than waiting for the October deadline. Past cycles have seen a surge in last-minute applications that overwhelmed the portal and caused technical failures. Institute verification must follow submission, and defective applications have only until November 15 to be corrected. The UGC helpline (0120-6619540, 8 AM to 8 PM) and the email helpdesk at helpdesk@nsp.gov.in are available for registration issues.
